logline: An orbit is a fall that keeps missing the ground.
purpose: A 24-second explainer for anyone who thinks satellites float.

shapes.name: One object, pushed further each time

shape: One ball, pushed further each time, until the ground curves away beneath it.

beats.motion: The ball drops onto a flat horizon and settles with one short spring; the line is the floor of everything after.

beats.beat: Throw it and it lands further
beats.onScreen: Throw it, and it lands further.
beats.motion: Two throws arc to the right, each landing further; each path stays as a faint line.
A harder throw; the camera pulls back with it in log zoom and the horizon becomes a planet.

beats.onScreen: Fast enough, and it never lands.
beats.motion: The fastest throw falls all the way round; the path closes into a ring.

beats.onScreen: An orbit is a fall that keeps missing.
beats.motion: Hold. The ball keeps going round; nothing else moves.

spine: One ball: it drops, is thrown, is thrown harder, and finally never lands. The horizon it lands on becomes the planet.
hold: The closed orbit with the claim beside it, still, 18.5–22 s.
bans: nothing enters from below for no reason
one accent: the ball and its path
sound: No narration; a quiet bed if one is added later.
look: Paper: an editorial explainer, Fraunces on cream, terracotta for the ball.
